lastPrompt: I want to experiment with converting the flow part of the dashboard to an interface where you can also create new components. Can you give a few suggestions on how we might design such an interface?

content.text:
Exploration is done — I have a clear picture of what exists. Here's the lay of the land, then a few design directions.

## What we're working with

- The flow view is a **React Flow** canvas (`web/src/components/FlowView.tsx`) that renders **only declared topology** — the JSON each system host emits from its `graph` verb (`dotnet run -- graph`). Nodes/edges are laid out deterministically; the canvas is strictly read-only today (no `onConnect`, no edit affordances).
- **Creation machinery already exists end-to-end**: the Templates tab posts to `POST /api/templates/{name}/create`, which runs `template.PrepareCreate`/`RunCreate` and writes the scaffold. The form renderer (`FormField` in `TemplatesView.tsx`) is generic over template `FieldSpec`s and directly reusable.
- Templates already carry `intropy.dev/block-kind` and `data-flow` labels, so a create-UI can offer "extractor / loader / transactional" as canvas-native concepts without new metadata.
- The key architectural tension: **the canvas draws truth derived from compiled hosts, but creating a component only writes a scaffold.** A new component won't appear in the declared topology until `sys create` re-assembles the host and the graph verb re-runs (a `dotnet build`, minutes not milliseconds). Every design below has to represent that gap honestly.

## Design directions

**A. Palette + drop, form in a drawer (the "diagramming tool" feel).** A left-hand palette of block kinds (filtered by template labels). Drag one into a system group; on drop, a side drawer opens with the existing template form, pre-filled with system context (name prefix, system path). Submit → existing create endpoint → the node renders immediately as a **ghost/draft node** ("scaffolded, not yet in topology") until a refresh confirms it. Most conventional and discoverable; medium effort. Main backend change: relax `resolveCreate` to allow validated multi-segment output paths (`root/<systemPath>/<name>`), plus serving labels on the template list endpoint.

**B. Connect-first ("draw the wire, get the right form").** Enable dragging a connection from a topic's out-handle (or a port) onto empty canvas. The gesture itself carries intent — "I want a subscriber to this topic" — so the UI can pre-filter templates by data-flow direction and pre-fill topic/pubsub/contract parameters. This is the most "flow-native" interaction and plays to your model where wiring is derived from scaffold values at `sys create` time. It's also the most work, and it only pays off if templates actually expose topic/connector choices as parameters the form can pre-fill.

**C. Draft mode with plan/apply (terraform-style).** A toggle switches the canvas into edit mode where you place several draft nodes and sketch edges purely client-side. A panel accumulates the pending creates as a reviewable list; "Apply" runs them sequentially, then triggers `sys create` re-assembly and one topology refresh at the end. This matches the reality that topology refresh is expensive (you batch it once instead of per-component) and fits your deterministic, records-never-lie ethos — the canvas never pretends a draft is real. Highest concept cost, but the best fit if creating a system usually means adding 3–5 components in one sitting, not one.

**D. Minimal contextual "+" (cheapest experiment).** No drag-drop at all: an "add component" button in the system group header or toolbar opens the existing template form pre-scoped to that system. The canvas stays read-only; you just remove the tab-switch friction. Almost pure re-composition of existing pieces — a good first experiment to validate the pre-fill and pending-node plumbing before investing in gestures.

**Common to all of them** (worth building once, regardless of direction): ghost-node rendering for scaffolded-but-not-yet-declared components (the join logic already exists — the flow view already matches scaffold dirs to topology component names), a way to trigger host re-assembly (`sys create` has no dashboard endpoint yet), and the multi-segment path validation in `resolveCreate`.

My take: **D is the right first experiment** (a day-ish of work, validates the whole pipeline), with **A as the destination** and C's batch-apply idea worth stealing if refresh latency proves annoying. B is beautiful but should wait until template parameters actually express wiring.

questions.question: Which design direction should I plan out for the experiment?

options.label: A: Palette + drag-drop
options.description: Block-kind palette, drag onto the canvas, form drawer on drop. The full diagramming-tool feel from the start.

options.label: C: Draft mode, plan/apply
options.description: Sketch several draft nodes client-side, review the pending creates, apply them as a batch with one topology refresh at the end.

options.label: B: Connect-first

options.label: Skip for now
options.description: Just create the scaffold; don't touch host re-assembly in this experiment at all.

message.content: What do you think about having placeholders that you can click on a map? Like having an extractor placeholder on the left, the core blocks in the middle and loader placeholders to the right?

content.text:
I think it's a strong idea — arguably better than the generic drag-drop palette, and it happens to fit this codebase unusually well. Here's why, and where the design decisions are.

## Why placeholder slots fit

**The left/middle/right semantics already exist in the metadata.** The flow view has a `KIND_DATA_FLOW` map (extractor→in, transactional→both, loader→out) used today only for card glyphs, and templates carry `intropy.dev/block-kind` + `intropy.dev/data-flow` labels. So a clicked placeholder knows exactly which templates to offer: the left slot filters the library to `block-kind: extractor`, the right slot to `loader`, the middle to `transactional-integration`. Zero new metadata needed — the placeholders make existing labels spatial.

**The layout engine cooperates.** Columns are assigned by longest-path layering, and `place(depth)` just takes the next free row in a column. A placeholder is one more node appended at the bottom of its column — no layout surgery. Extractors naturally land in column 0 and loaders at the end already, so the placeholders sit where their kind's real nodes live.

**It teaches the golden path.** This is the part I like most: an empty system stops being a blank "no topology" message and becomes the archetype's shape — in → process → out with three clickable slots. The canvas itself communicates "an integration looks like this, fill in the blanks," which is very aligned with Intropy's opinionated-blueprint model. Drag-drop says "arrange whatever you want"; slots say "here's the pattern."

**It sidesteps drag-drop entirely.** Click placeholder → side drawer opens with the existing template form (the `FormField` renderer from the Templates tab), pre-filtered to that block kind and pre-scoped to the system. On submit, the placeholder itself becomes the ghost node ("scaffolded, awaiting topology") — a clean lifecycle: slot → ghost → confirmed node.

## The design decisions this raises

1. **Always visible vs. edit mode.** Always-on placeholders add noise when you're using the flow view for monitoring/reading. Options: a subtle "+" slot per column that's low-contrast until hover; or an explicit "add components" toggle that reveals the slots. I lean toward the subtle always-on version for the experiment — a mode toggle is one more concept, and dashed low-contrast slots are a well-understood idiom.

2. **One slot per column vs. slot-per-gap.** Simplest: one placeholder at the bottom of each of the three kind-columns. Fancier: placeholders between existing nodes implying wiring position — but wiring is derived from scaffold values at `sys create` time, not from canvas position, so positional slots would imply something the system doesn't honor. One-per-column is honest.

3. **Middle column contents.** With minimal topology scope, middle = transactional (aggregator is cut). If multiple kinds ever map there, the middle slot's drawer just lists more templates — the design absorbs that.

4. **The empty-system case** is where this shines — but note today the flow view only renders systems that have a declared topology. Showing the slot skeleton for a system that has scaffolds but no host yet (or nothing at all) would need the system picker to include scaffold-only systems. Worth including — it's the best onboarding moment.

The host re-sync question from before still stands: after a slot-create, does the dashboard run `sys create` + topology refresh automatically, or show the ghost with a "refresh to declare" prompt?

# Feature: creating components from the dashboard flow view via placeholder slots

The dashboard (`intropy dashboard`, React 18 + TypeScript + Vite SPA in web/, Go stdlib server in internal/dashboard/) has a flow view (web/src/components/FlowView.tsx) rendering declared topology (topology.intropy.io/v1, emitted by each system host's `dotnet run -- graph` verb) on a React Flow canvas (@xyflow/react v12). **Agreed design:**
1. **Placeholder slots on the canvas**: subtle, always-visible, low-contrast dashed placeholder nodes — one at the bottom of each kind-column: extractor slot on the left (column 0), transactional ("core") slot in the middle, loader slot on the right. 3. **Host re-sync is manual with prompt**: after a create, show ghost node(s) plus a banner offering "re-assemble & refresh" (i.e., the user or a future endpoint runs `sys create` + POST /api/topology/refresh). - The `nodeId` join: a topology component name is matched to a scaffolded integration path by directory basename (FlowView.tsx:398-407); IntegrationDetail comes from /api/flow.

Keep resolveCreate's security posture.
   - Getting block-kind labels to the palette efficiently (extend listTemplates to include labels from Describe — check cost; the library is already fetched once).

# Implementation Plan: Create-from-canvas via placeholder slots in the Flow view

All file references verified against the current tree on `feature/v-next`.

## Verified facts the plan relies on

- `GET /api/flow` (handlers.go:265) already carries everything ghost rendering needs: `integrationSummary` embeds `template.ScaffoldEntry` → `Scaffold`, so each row has `blockKind`, `dataFlow`, `systemPath`, `path`. **No flow-payload change is needed for ghosts.**
- The FlowView system picker is already derived from `/api/flow` grouping by `systemPath` (FlowView.tsx:185-206), so any system with ≥1 block scaffold already appears even without topology — the gap is (a) it renders the "No declared topology" empty state, and (b) a **host-only** system (fresh `sys` scaffold, zero blocks) never appears, because `scan()` (handlers.go:185) filters `RoleSystemHost`/`RoleSharedLibrary` out of the entries.
- `GET /api/templates` returns names only (`lib.List()`); labels live on `Library.Describe(name)` (library.go:154-172), which after `fetchLibrary` is **pure local-disk reads on the extracted tarball** — per-name Describe in the list handler is cheap.
- Block-kind constants (scaffold.go:50-53): `extractor`, `loader`, `transactional-integration`. Labels: `intropy.dev/block-kind`, `intropy.dev/data-flow`.
- `resolveCreate` (templates.go:182-219) is the security boundary: single-segment name + absolute-path equality assertion.
- No JS test runner exists (package.json: only `tsc -b && vite build`); Go handler tests use `testHandlerWith`, `writeScaffold`/`writeScaffoldRole`, `newTemplateLibraryServer`, `postJSON`, `get` helpers. **No fixture workspace in testdata** — dashboard tests build workspaces with `t.TempDir()` + `writeScaffold`.
- The topology↔scaffold join is `joinProject(topo.path, c.name)` matched against `it.path` (FlowView.tsx:398-407); ghosts are exactly the reverse set.

---

## Phase 1 — Backend: create into a system directory

### 1.1 Extend `createRequest` with an optional `dir`

`internal/dashboard/templates.go`:

```go
type createRequest struct {
    Name string `json:"name"`
    // Dir is the root-relative, slash-separated directory the output is
    // rendered under ("" or "." means the workspace root — today's behavior).
    // It must already exist: the endpoint scaffolds into systems, it does
    // not invent directory trees.
    Dir    string         `json:"dir,omitempty"`
    Values map[string]any `json:"values"`
    Force  bool           `json:"force,omitempty"`
}
```

### 1.2 Extend `resolveCreate` — validation rules spelled out

Keep the existing name rule untouched, add dir handling before the join:

1. `Name`: unchanged — non-empty, no `/` or `\`, not `.`/`..` (existing lines 186-188).
2. Normalize `Dir`: `""` → `"."`. If `"."`, behavior is byte-for-byte today's (`filepath.Join(s.root, req.Name)`), so existing clients/tests are unaffected.
3. - `onCreated(outputDir)`: re-fetch `api.flow().then(setGraph)` (the new scaffold then appears as a ghost via the normal join — the "placeholder → ghost transition" is just data), keep the drawer open showing the success line or close it (recommend: close, the ghost + banner are the confirmation).
- **Re-sync banner** (decision: minimal — show the command, button only refreshes): when `ghosts.length > 0` for the selected system, render above the canvas:
  > *N scaffolded component(s) are not in the declared topology yet. Run `intropy sys create` in `<systemPath>` to re-assemble the host, then refresh.* — [Refresh topology]
  The button reuses the existing `refresh()` (POST `/api/topology/refresh`). No auto-run of `sys create`. Class `banner hint` (new variant) so it doesn't read as an error.

---

## Phase 4 — CreateDrawer

New `web/src/components/CreateDrawer.tsx`, rendered inside `.flow-canvas` (same absolute-right positioning pattern as `.flow-detail`, index.css:1014):

Props: `{ kind, systemPath, systemLabel, onClose, onCreated: (outputDir: string) => void }`.

- On mount: `api.listTemplates()`; filter `list.entries` by `labels['intropy.dev/block-kind'] === kindLabel` where `kindLabel` is `extractor` / `transactional-integration` / `loader` (match `BlockKindTransactional` exactly; normalize-compare hyphens like `dataFlowFor` does for safety). Empty result → explicit empty state naming the label, with a "show all templates" escape hatch (one boolean) — the official library's labeling can't be verified from this repo (open question below).
- Template select (reuse `Combobox`), then the `TemplatePanel` form pattern: `api.getTemplate(name)`, seed defaults, `missing` computed identically, `FormField`/`Field` from `form.tsx`, out-dir name input, plus a **locked** row showing the destination: `<systemPath>/` prefix rendered read-only before the name input.
- Submit: `api.createTemplate(tpl, { name, values, force, dir: systemPath })` — where FlowView passes `'.'` for the workspace pseudo-system (`WORKSPACE_KEY` → `'.'`, mirroring `topologyFor`). 409 → force checkbox (copy the existing `CreateState` union and 409 branch). 201 → `onCreated(result.outputDir)`.

Keep `TemplatesView` untouched apart from the form.tsx imports — the drawer is a parallel consumer, not a refactor of `TemplatePanel` (they differ in: pre-filter, locked dir, no "view in catalog" CTA; sharing `FormField`/`Field` is the right granularity).

## Phase 5 — CSS (`web/src/index.css`)

Following the `.rf-*` block (from line 1322):

- `.rf-slot`: dashed 1.5px `var(--border)`, transparent/`--bg` fill, `color: var(--text-muted)`, low opacity (~0.6), `border-radius` matching `.rf-int`, transition; `.rf-slot:hover` → full opacity, `border-color: var(--text-muted)`, subtle surface fill. Both themes come free from the vars; spot-check dark since dashed low-contrast lines can vanish on dark backgrounds — may need a `:root[data-theme='dark'] .rf-slot` opacity tweak (precedent at line 1739).
- `.rf-int.ghost`: dashed border, ~0.65 opacity, muted name; small "scaffolded" tag styled like `.rf-int-tag`.
- `.create-drawer`: clone `.flow-detail`'s geometry (absolute right, `z-index: 10`), plus form spacing (reuse `.template-form` rules where selectors allow).
- `.banner.hint`: neutral/info variant of `.banner`; inline `<code>` styling for the `sys create` command.

---

## Sequencing (each step independently verifiable)

1. **Backend create-into-dir** (1.1, 1.2, 1.5 create tests) — `go test ./internal/dashboard/`; verifiable via `curl` against a running dashboard.
2. **Backend list labels + /api/systems** (1.3, 1.4, remaining tests) — additive, existing web build keeps working.
3. **Frontend plumbing** (Phase 2) — `make web` green, zero visual change.
4. **FlowView ghosts + slots + skeleton** (Phase 3, slot click a no-op) — visually verifiable read-only; ghosts already demonstrable by hand-writing a `.intropy/scaffold.json` beside a system.
5. **CreateDrawer + wiring + banner** (Phase 4 + 3.6 wiring).
6. **CSS polish, light/dark pass** (Phase 5).

## Verification

- Go: `go test ./internal/dashboard/ ./internal/template/`.
- Web: `make web` (runs `tsc -b && vite build`) — the only automated JS gate; there is **no JS test runner** (confirmed in web/package.json).
- Manual: there is **no fixture workspace in testdata** (confirmed by find). Build a scratch one: `mkdir /tmp/ws && cd /tmp/ws`, hand-write `acme/erp/erp-host/.intropy/scaffold.json` with `"role":"system-host"` plus a couple of block scaffolds with `"blockKind":"extractor"` etc. (5-line JSON each, matching `writeScaffoldRole`'s shape) — this exercises scaffold-only systems, ghosts, slots, and the drawer end-to-end without dotnet. Run `intropy dashboard` in it (serves :8730) and `make web-dev` for the HMR proxy. Full topology confirmation (ghost → declared after `sys create` + Refresh) needs a real dotnet system host — verify once against a real workspace.

## Risks / open questions

1. **Do the official library's templates carry `intropy.dev/block-kind` labels?** Unverifiable from this repo (labels live in the templates repo). The drawer's strict filter could show an empty list in production — hence the "show all" escape hatch. Worth checking one library release before building the filter UX.
2. **Middle-column semantics**: the "transactional" slot column is a heuristic (`round(loaderCol/2)` clamped); in graphs where topics occupy the middle columns the slot lands beside topics, not components. Acceptable for an experiment; flag in the PR.
3. **Host-only + topology-less vs. topology-errored systems**: a host whose graph verb *fails* appears in `report.errors` and gets the skeleton treatment too (declared undefined). The error banner already shows why — acceptable, but the skeleton could be misread as "empty system"; the existing errors banner mitigates.
4. **Symlinked dir escape** in `resolveCreate` is theoretical (local single-user tool, same posture as today's name handling); `EvalSymlinks` hardening is one line if wanted.
5. **Workspace pseudo-system**: slots there scaffold at the root (`dir: "."`), which equals today's Templates-view behavior — fine, but the "system" label in the drawer should say "Workspace".
6. `entries` on `/api/templates` slightly departs from "mirrors `template list -o json`" — kept additive with `templates` untouched; consider back-porting a `--detailed` flag to the CLI later if the mirror matters.

# Flow view: create components via placeholder slots

## Context

The dashboard's flow view (`web/src/components/FlowView.tsx`) is a read-only React Flow canvas rendering declared topology from each system host's `graph` verb. Creation lives in a separate Templates tab. This experiment converts the flow view into a create surface using **placeholder slots**: subtle, always-visible dashed slot nodes — extractor on the left column, transactional ("core") in the middle, loader on the right — that open a pre-filtered create drawer when clicked. The slot arrangement makes the golden-path shape (in → process → out) visible, and an empty system renders as a fillable skeleton instead of a "no topology" message.

Decisions made with the user:
- **Slots are subtle always-on** (low-contrast dashed, brighten on hover) — no edit-mode toggle.
- **Host re-sync is manual with a prompt**: after a create, the new component renders as a *ghost node* (scaffolded, not yet declared) plus a banner showing the `intropy sys create` hint and a "Refresh topology" button. No auto-run of `sys create` in this experiment.
- **Scaffold-only / host-only systems appear in the picker** and render as the three-slot skeleton plus ghosts.

Everything reuses the existing create pipeline: `POST /api/templates/{name}/create` → `template.PrepareCreate`/`RunCreate` (`internal/dashboard/templates.go`, `internal/template/prepare.go`), and the form renderer `FormField`/`Field` from `web/src/components/TemplatesView.tsx`. Template labels `intropy.dev/block-kind` / `intropy.dev/data-flow` (constants in `internal/template/scaffold.go:24-53`) drive slot→template filtering — no new metadata.

## Phase 1 — Backend: create into a system directory

**`internal/dashboard/templates.go`**

1. Add optional `Dir string` to `createRequest` (root-relative, slash-separated; `""`/`"."` = workspace root, byte-for-byte today's behavior).
2. Extend `resolveCreate` (lines 182-219), keeping its security posture:
   - `Name` rule unchanged (single segment, no `/` `\` `.` `..`).
   - Split `Dir` on `/`; reject empty segments, `.`, `..`, segments starting with `.`, any `\`.
   - `outputDir = filepath.Join(s.root, filepath.FromSlash(dir), req.Name)`; keep the absolute-equality escape assertion generalized over the segments.
   - The dir must `os.Stat` as an existing directory under root → 422 otherwise. Do **not** require a known system scaffold in it (would block first-block-into-hand-made-dir; writes are confined under root regardless).
   - No response change: `result.OutputDir` already goes through `s.relPath`, giving the client the `/api/flow` identifier space it needs for the ghost join.
3. `listTemplates` (line 77): after `lib.List()`, loop `lib.Describe(name)` (cheap — local reads on the extracted tarball) and add an **additive** `entries` array of `{name, title, description, labels}`; keep `templates` untouched. Skip (don't 502) a template whose Describe fails.

**`internal/dashboard/handlers.go`**

4. New `GET /api/systems` handler reusing `scan()`'s systems map (which already sees `RoleSystemHost` scaffolds it filters from integration listings) → `[{path, name}]` sorted, always an array. This surfaces host-only systems (zero blocks) to the picker.

**Tests** (`internal/dashboard/templates_test.go` etc., following existing `testHandlerWith`/`writeScaffoldRole`/`postJSON` patterns):
- Happy path: create into pre-existing `acme/erp`, assert 201 + `outputDir == "acme/erp/orders"` + files on disk.
- Table-driven dir validation: `"../x"`, `"a/../b"`, `"/etc"`, `"a\\b"`, `"a//b"`, `".hidden/x"`, missing dir (422), `"."` (≡ omitted); assert nothing lands outside root.
- Labels present in `entries`; `GET /api/systems` with host-only scaffold and with empty workspace.

## Phase 2 — Frontend plumbing (no visual change)

- **`web/src/api.ts`**: `dir?: string` on `CreateRequest`; `entries?: TemplateSummary[]` (`{name, title?, description?, labels?}`) on the template list type; `SystemInfo {path, name}` + `api.systems()`.
- **New `web/src/components/form.tsx`**: move `FormField`, `Field`, `isEmpty` verbatim out of `TemplatesView.tsx`; import back. Zero behavior change; gate with `make web`.

## Phase 3 — FlowView: slots, ghosts, skeleton systems

All in `web/src/components/FlowView.tsx`, inside/around `buildDeclaredGraph` (lines 379-626).

- **Columns**: after depth assignment, `effCols = max(cols, 3)` so thin/empty graphs get a 3-column skeleton (`groupWidth`, `rowsInCol` use `effCols`). Slot columns: extractor → 0; loader → `max(2, maxDepth)`; transactional → clamped middle (`min(loaderCol-1, max(1, round(loaderCol/2)))`). Ghosts map by scaffold `blockKind`: `extractor`→left, `loader`→right, else middle.
- **Emission order** does bottom-of-column placement for free via `place()`: components → topics (unchanged) → ghosts → slots, all **before** the `maxRows`/`groupHeight` computation (~line 515) so the group boundary contains them.
- **Ghosts** = reverse of the existing join at lines 398-407: `items` whose `path` isn't in `{joinProject(topo.path, c.name)}`. Rendered with the existing `integration` node type + `ghost: true` data flag (class `rf-int ghost`, "scaffolded" tag, `dataFlow` from the scaffold). Node id = `it.path`, so the existing `onNodeClick` → catalog selection works unmodified. `/api/flow` already carries `blockKind`/`dataFlow`/`systemPath` per integration — no payload change.
- **Slot node type**: new `SlotNode` in `NODE_TYPES` (`data: {kind}`, not draggable/selectable, `NODE_W × NODE_H`, no handles, label "+ Extractor" etc.). `onNodeClick`: `node.type === 'slot'` → open drawer.
- **Scaffold-only/host-only systems**: fetch `api.systems()` alongside `api.flow()`; merge unseen paths into the system picker. When a selected system has no declared topology, feed a synthetic `{path, system, components: []}` through the same `buildDeclaredGraph` — all items become ghosts, three slots render, skeleton falls out. Guard the `FlowDetail` inspector behind `declared` (no topics/ports exist).
- **Re-sync banner**: when the selected system has ghosts, render above the canvas: "*N scaffolded component(s) not in the declared topology yet. Run `intropy sys create` in `<systemPath>`, then refresh.*" with a button reusing the existing `refresh()` (`POST /api/topology/refresh`). New neutral `banner hint` styling.
- **After create**: close the drawer, re-fetch `api.flow()` — the new scaffold appears as a ghost through the normal join (placeholder→ghost is pure data).

## Phase 4 — CreateDrawer

New `web/src/components/CreateDrawer.tsx`, positioned like `.flow-detail` (absolute right inside `.flow-canvas`). Props: `{kind, systemPath, systemLabel, onClose, onCreated}`.

- Filter `list.entries` by `labels['intropy.dev/block-kind']` ∈ {`extractor`, `transactional-integration`, `loader`} per slot kind (hyphen-normalized compare like `dataFlowFor`). Empty result → explicit message + "show all templates" escape hatch (the official library's labeling isn't verifiable from this repo).
- Template picker via existing `Combobox`; then the `TemplatePanel` pattern: `api.getTemplate`, seed defaults, `missing` required computation, `FormField`/`Field` from `form.tsx`, name input with a **locked read-only `<systemPath>/` prefix** showing the destination.
- Submit: `api.createTemplate(tpl, {name, values, force, dir: systemPath})` (workspace pseudo-system passes `'.'`, labeled "Workspace"). 409 → force checkbox, same as TemplatesView. 201 → `onCreated(result.outputDir)`.
- `TemplatesView` stays untouched apart from `form.tsx` imports — the drawer is a parallel consumer, not a refactor.

## Phase 5 — CSS (`web/src/index.css`, following the `.rf-*` block from ~line 1322)

- `.rf-slot`: 1.5px dashed `var(--border)`, muted text, ~0.6 opacity → full opacity + surface fill on hover. Spot-check dark theme (dashed low-contrast lines vanish easily; per-theme tweak precedent exists ~line 1739).
- `.rf-int.ghost`: dashed border, ~0.65 opacity, "scaffolded" tag.
- `.create-drawer` cloning `.flow-detail` geometry; `.banner.hint` neutral variant with inline `code` styling.

## Sequencing (each step verifiable alone)

1. Backend create-into-dir + tests → `go test ./internal/dashboard/`.
2. Backend template labels + `/api/systems` + tests (additive; existing web build unaffected).
3. Frontend plumbing (`api.ts`, `form.tsx`) → `make web` green, no visual change.
4. FlowView ghosts + slots + skeleton (slot click no-op) — read-only, visually verifiable.
5. CreateDrawer + wiring + banner.
6. CSS polish, light/dark pass.

Good commit points after steps 2, 4, and 6 (propose, don't auto-commit).

## Verification

- Go: `go test ./internal/dashboard/ ./internal/template/`.
- Web: `make web` (`tsc -b && vite build`) — the only automated JS gate; no JS test runner exists.
- Manual, no dotnet needed: build a scratch workspace (no fixture exists in testdata) — hand-write `acme/erp/erp-host/.intropy/scaffold.json` with `"role":"system-host"` plus a couple of block scaffolds with `blockKind` set (shape matches `writeScaffoldRole` in the dashboard tests). Run `intropy dashboard` there + `make web-dev` (HMR proxy to :8730). This exercises scaffold-only systems, ghosts, slots, and the drawer end-to-end.
- Full loop (ghost → declared after `sys create` + Refresh) once against a real dotnet workspace.

## Risks / open questions

1. **Template labels in the official library**: whether released templates actually carry `intropy.dev/block-kind` isn't verifiable from this repo — the "show all" escape hatch covers it; check one release early.

# Flow view: create components via placeholder slots

## Context

The dashboard's flow view (`web/src/components/FlowView.tsx`) is a read-only React Flow canvas rendering declared topology from each system host's `graph` verb. Creation lives in a separate Templates tab. This experiment converts the flow view into a create surface using **placeholder slots**: subtle, always-visible dashed slot nodes — extractor on the left column, transactional ("core") in the middle, loader on the right — that open a pre-filtered create drawer when clicked. The slot arrangement makes the golden-path shape (in → process → out) visible, and an empty system renders as a fillable skeleton instead of a "no topology" message.

Decisions made with the user:
- **Slots are subtle always-on** (low-contrast dashed, brighten on hover) — no edit-mode toggle.
- **Host re-sync is manual with a prompt**: after a create, the new component renders as a *ghost node* (scaffolded, not yet declared) plus a banner showing the `intropy sys create` hint and a "Refresh topology" button. No auto-run of `sys create` in this experiment.
- **Scaffold-only / host-only systems appear in the picker** and render as the three-slot skeleton plus ghosts.

Everything reuses the existing create pipeline: `POST /api/templates/{name}/create` → `template.PrepareCreate`/`RunCreate` (`internal/dashboard/templates.go`, `internal/template/prepare.go`), and the form renderer `FormField`/`Field` from `web/src/components/TemplatesView.tsx`. Template labels `intropy.dev/block-kind` / `intropy.dev/data-flow` (constants in `internal/template/scaffold.go:24-53`) drive slot→template filtering — no new metadata.

## Phase 1 — Backend: create into a system directory

**`internal/dashboard/templates.go`**

1. Add optional `Dir string` to `createRequest` (root-relative, slash-separated; `""`/`"."` = workspace root, byte-for-byte today's behavior).
2. Extend `resolveCreate` (lines 182-219), keeping its security posture:
   - `Name` rule unchanged (single segment, no `/` `\` `.` `..`).
   - Split `Dir` on `/`; reject empty segments, `.`, `..`, segments starting with `.`, any `\`.
   - `outputDir = filepath.Join(s.root, filepath.FromSlash(dir), req.Name)`; keep the absolute-equality escape assertion generalized over the segments.
   - The dir must `os.Stat` as an existing directory under root → 422 otherwise. Do **not** require a known system scaffold in it (would block first-block-into-hand-made-dir; writes are confined under root regardless).
   - No response change: `result.OutputDir` already goes through `s.relPath`, giving the client the `/api/flow` identifier space it needs for the ghost join.
3. `listTemplates` (line 77): after `lib.List()`, loop `lib.Describe(name)` (cheap — local reads on the extracted tarball) and add an **additive** `entries` array of `{name, title, description, labels}`; keep `templates` untouched. Skip (don't 502) a template whose Describe fails.

**`internal/dashboard/handlers.go`**

4. New `GET /api/systems` handler reusing `scan()`'s systems map (which already sees `RoleSystemHost` scaffolds it filters from integration listings) → `[{path, name}]` sorted, always an array. This surfaces host-only systems (zero blocks) to the picker.

**Tests** (`internal/dashboard/templates_test.go` etc., following existing `testHandlerWith`/`writeScaffoldRole`/`postJSON` patterns):
- Happy path: create into pre-existing `acme/erp`, assert 201 + `outputDir == "acme/erp/orders"` + files on disk.
- Table-driven dir validation: `"../x"`, `"a/../b"`, `"/etc"`, `"a\\b"`, `"a//b"`, `".hidden/x"`, missing dir (422), `"."` (≡ omitted); assert nothing lands outside root.
- Labels present in `entries`; `GET /api/systems` with host-only scaffold and with empty workspace.

## Phase 2 — Frontend plumbing (no visual change)

- **`web/src/api.ts`**: `dir?: string` on `CreateRequest`; `entries?: TemplateSummary[]` (`{name, title?, description?, labels?}`) on the template list type; `SystemInfo {path, name}` + `api.systems()`.
- **New `web/src/components/form.tsx`**: move `FormField`, `Field`, `isEmpty` verbatim out of `TemplatesView.tsx`; import back. Zero behavior change; gate with `make web`.

## Phase 3 — FlowView: slots, ghosts, skeleton systems

All in `web/src/components/FlowView.tsx`, inside/around `buildDeclaredGraph` (lines 379-626).

- **Columns**: after depth assignment, `effCols = max(cols, 3)` so thin/empty graphs get a 3-column skeleton (`groupWidth`, `rowsInCol` use `effCols`). Slot columns: extractor → 0; loader → `max(2, maxDepth)`; transactional → clamped middle (`min(loaderCol-1, max(1, round(loaderCol/2)))`). Ghosts map by scaffold `blockKind`: `extractor`→left, `loader`→right, else middle.
- **Emission order** does bottom-of-column placement for free via `place()`: components → topics (unchanged) → ghosts → slots, all **before** the `maxRows`/`groupHeight` computation (~line 515) so the group boundary contains them.
- **Ghosts** = reverse of the existing join at lines 398-407: `items` whose `path` isn't in `{joinProject(topo.path, c.name)}`. Rendered with the existing `integration` node type + `ghost: true` data flag (class `rf-int ghost`, "scaffolded" tag, `dataFlow` from the scaffold). Node id = `it.path`, so the existing `onNodeClick` → catalog selection works unmodified. `/api/flow` already carries `blockKind`/`dataFlow`/`systemPath` per integration — no payload change.
- **Slot node type**: new `SlotNode` in `NODE_TYPES` (`data: {kind}`, not draggable/selectable, `NODE_W × NODE_H`, no handles, label "+ Extractor" etc.). `onNodeClick`: `node.type === 'slot'` → open drawer.
- **Scaffold-only/host-only systems**: fetch `api.systems()` alongside `api.flow()`; merge unseen paths into the system picker. When a selected system has no declared topology, feed a synthetic `{path, system, components: []}` through the same `buildDeclaredGraph` — all items become ghosts, three slots render, skeleton falls out. Guard the `FlowDetail` inspector behind `declared` (no topics/ports exist).
- **Re-sync banner**: when the selected system has ghosts, render above the canvas: "*N scaffolded component(s) not in the declared topology yet. Run `intropy sys create` in `<systemPath>`, then refresh.*" with a button reusing the existing `refresh()` (`POST /api/topology/refresh`). New neutral `banner hint` styling.
- **After create**: close the drawer, re-fetch `api.flow()` — the new scaffold appears as a ghost through the normal join (placeholder→ghost is pure data).

## Phase 4 — CreateDrawer

New `web/src/components/CreateDrawer.tsx`, positioned like `.flow-detail` (absolute right inside `.flow-canvas`). Props: `{kind, systemPath, systemLabel, onClose, onCreated}`.

- Filter `list.entries` by `labels['intropy.dev/block-kind']` ∈ {`extractor`, `transactional-integration`, `loader`} per slot kind (hyphen-normalized compare like `dataFlowFor`). Empty result → explicit message + "show all templates" escape hatch (the official library's labeling isn't verifiable from this repo).
- Template picker via existing `Combobox`; then the `TemplatePanel` pattern: `api.getTemplate`, seed defaults, `missing` required computation, `FormField`/`Field` from `form.tsx`, name input with a **locked read-only `<systemPath>/` prefix** showing the destination.
- Submit: `api.createTemplate(tpl, {name, values, force, dir: systemPath})` (workspace pseudo-system passes `'.'`, labeled "Workspace"). 409 → force checkbox, same as TemplatesView. 201 → `onCreated(result.outputDir)`.
- `TemplatesView` stays untouched apart from `form.tsx` imports — the drawer is a parallel consumer, not a refactor.

## Phase 5 — CSS (`web/src/index.css`, following the `.rf-*` block from ~line 1322)

- `.rf-slot`: 1.5px dashed `var(--border)`, muted text, ~0.6 opacity → full opacity + surface fill on hover. Spot-check dark theme (dashed low-contrast lines vanish easily; per-theme tweak precedent exists ~line 1739).
- `.rf-int.ghost`: dashed border, ~0.65 opacity, "scaffolded" tag.
- `.create-drawer` cloning `.flow-detail` geometry; `.banner.hint` neutral variant with inline `code` styling.

## Sequencing (each step verifiable alone)

1. Backend create-into-dir + tests → `go test ./internal/dashboard/`.
2. Backend template labels + `/api/systems` + tests (additive; existing web build unaffected).
3. Frontend plumbing (`api.ts`, `form.tsx`) → `make web` green, no visual change.
4. FlowView ghosts + slots + skeleton (slot click no-op) — read-only, visually verifiable.
5. CreateDrawer + wiring + banner.
6. CSS polish, light/dark pass.

Good commit points after steps 2, 4, and 6 (propose, don't auto-commit).

## Verification

- Go: `go test ./internal/dashboard/ ./internal/template/`.
- Web: `make web` (`tsc -b && vite build`) — the only automated JS gate; no JS test runner exists.
- Manual, no dotnet needed: build a scratch workspace (no fixture exists in testdata) — hand-write `acme/erp/erp-host/.intropy/scaffold.json` with `"role":"system-host"` plus a couple of block scaffolds with `blockKind` set (shape matches `writeScaffoldRole` in the dashboard tests). - Full loop (ghost → declared after `sys create` + Refresh) once against a real dotnet workspace.

## Risks / open questions

2. **Middle-column heuristic**: in wide graphs the transactional slot may land beside topic nodes; acceptable for the experiment.

The slot arrangement makes the golden-path shape (in → process → out) visible, and an empty system renders as a fillable skeleton instead of a "no topology" message.

Decisions made with the user:
- **Slots are subtle always-on** (low-contrast dashed, brighten on hover) — no edit-mode toggle.
- **Host re-sync is manual with a prompt**: after a create, the new component renders as a *ghost node* (scaffolded, not yet declared) plus a banner showing the `intropy sys create` hint and a "Refresh topology" button. No auto-run of `sys create` in this experiment.
- **Scaffold-only / host-only systems appear in the picker** and render as the three-slot skeleton plus ghosts.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/robinhultman/.claude/skills/golang-cli

**Persona:** You are a Go CLI engineer. You build tools that feel native to the Unix shell — composable, scriptable, and predictable under automation.

**Modes:**

- **Build** — creating a new CLI from scratch: follow the project structure, root command setup, flag binding, and version embedding sections sequentially.
- **Extend** — adding subcommands, flags, or completions to an existing CLI: read the current command tree first, then apply changes consistent with the existing structure.
- **Review** — auditing an existing CLI for correctness: check the Common Mistakes table, verify `SilenceUsage`/`SilenceErrors`, flag-to-Viper binding, exit codes, and stdout/stderr discipline.

# Go CLI Best Practices

Use Cobra + Viper as the default stack for Go CLI applications. Cobra provides the command/subcommand/flag structure and Viper handles configuration from files, environment variables, and flags with automatic layering. This combination powers kubectl, docker, gh, hugo, and most production Go CLIs.

When using Cobra or Viper, refer to the library's official documentation and code examples for current API signatures.

For trivial single-purpose tools with no subcommands and few flags, stdlib `flag` is sufficient.

## Quick Reference

| Concern             | Package / Tool                       |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Commands & flags    | `github.com/spf13/cobra`             |
| Configuration       | `github.com/spf13/viper`             |
| Flag parsing        | `github.com/spf13/pflag` (via Cobra) |
| Colored output      | `github.com/fatih/color`             |
| Table output        | `github.com/olekukonko/tablewriter`  |
| Interactive prompts | `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea` |
| Version injection   | `go build -ldflags`                  |
| Distribution        | `goreleaser`                         |

## Project Structure

Organize CLI commands in `cmd/myapp/` with one file per command. Keep `main.go` minimal — it only calls `Execute()`.

```
myapp/
├── cmd/
│   └── myapp/
│       ├── main.go              # package main, only calls Execute()
│       ├── root.go              # Root command + Viper init
│       ├── serve.go             # "serve" subcommand
│       ├── migrate.go           # "migrate" subcommand
│       └── version.go           # "version" subcommand
├── go.mod
└── go.sum
```

`main.go` should be minimal — see [assets/examples/main.go](assets/examples/main.go).

## Root Command Setup

The root command initializes Viper configuration and sets up global behavior via `PersistentPreRunE`. See [assets/examples/root.go](assets/examples/root.go).

Key points:

- `SilenceUsage: true` MUST be set — prevents printing the full usage text on every error
- `SilenceErrors: true` MUST be set — lets you control error output format yourself
- `PersistentPreRunE` runs before every subcommand, so config is always initialized
- Logs go to stderr, output goes to stdout

## Subcommands

Add subcommands by creating separate files in `cmd/myapp/` and registering them in `init()`. See [assets/examples/serve.go](assets/examples/serve.go) for a complete subcommand example including command groups.

## Flags

See [assets/examples/flags.go](assets/examples/flags.go) for all flag patterns:

### Persistent vs Local

- **Persistent** flags are inherited by all subcommands (e.g., `--config`)
- **Local** flags only apply to the command they're defined on (e.g., `--port`)

### Required Flags

Use `MarkFlagRequired`, `MarkFlagsMutuallyExclusive`, and `MarkFlagsOneRequired` for flag constraints.

### Flag Validation with RegisterFlagCompletionFunc

Provide completion suggestions for flag values.

### Always Bind Flags to Viper

This ensures `viper.GetInt("port")` returns the flag value, env var `MYAPP_PORT`, or config file value — whichever has highest precedence.

## Argument Validation

Cobra provides built-in validators for positional arguments. See [assets/examples/args.go](assets/examples/args.go) for both built-in and custom validation examples.

| Validator                   | Description                          |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `cobra.NoArgs`              | Fails if any args provided           |
| `cobra.ExactArgs(n)`        | Requires exactly n args              |
| `cobra.MinimumNArgs(n)`     | Requires at least n args             |
| `cobra.MaximumNArgs(n)`     | Allows at most n args                |
| `cobra.RangeArgs(min, max)` | Requires between min and max         |
| `cobra.ExactValidArgs(n)`   | Exactly n args, must be in ValidArgs |

## Configuration with Viper

Viper resolves configuration values in this order (highest to lowest precedence):

1. **CLI flags** (explicit user input)
2. **Environment variables** (deployment config)
3. **Config file** (persistent settings)
4. **Defaults** (set in code)

See [assets/examples/config.go](assets/examples/config.go) for complete Viper integration including struct unmarshaling and config file watching.

### Example Config File (.myapp.yaml)

```yaml
port: 8080
host: localhost
log-level: info
database:
  dsn: postgres://localhost:5432/myapp
  max-conn: 25
```

With the setup above, these are all equivalent:

- Flag: `--port 9090`
- Env var: `MYAPP_PORT=9090`
- Config file: `port: 9090`

## Version and Build Info

Version SHOULD be embedded at compile time using `ldflags`. See [assets/examples/version.go](assets/examples/version.go) for the version command and build instructions.

## Exit Codes

Exit codes MUST follow Unix conventions:

| Code  | Meaning           | When to Use                               |
| ----- | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| 0     | Success           | Operation completed normally              |
| 1     | General error     | Runtime failure                           |
| 2     | Usage error       | Invalid flags or arguments                |
| 64-78 | BSD sysexits      | Specific error categories                 |
| 126   | Cannot execute    | Permission denied                         |
| 127   | Command not found | Missing dependency                        |
| 128+N | Signal N          | Terminated by signal (e.g., 130 = SIGINT) |

See [assets/examples/exit_codes.go](assets/examples/exit_codes.go) for a pattern mapping errors to exit codes.

## I/O Patterns

See [assets/examples/output.go](assets/examples/output.go) for all I/O patterns:

- **stdout vs stderr**: NEVER write diagnostic output to stdout — stdout is for program output (pipeable), stderr for logs/errors/diagnostics
- **Detecting pipe vs terminal**: check `os.ModeCharDevice` on stdout
- **Machine-readable output**: support `--output` flag for table/json/plain formats
- **Colors**: use `fatih/color` which auto-disables when output is not a terminal

## Signal Handling

Signal handling MUST use `signal.NotifyContext` to propagate cancellation through context. See [assets/examples/signal.go](assets/examples/signal.go) for graceful HTTP server shutdown.

## Shell Completions

Cobra generates completions for bash, zsh, fish, and PowerShell automatically. See [assets/examples/completion.go](assets/examples/completion.go) for both the completion command and custom flag/argument completions.

## Testing CLI Commands

Test commands by executing them programmatically and capturing output. See [assets/examples/cli_test.go](assets/examples/cli_test.go).

Use `cmd.OutOrStdout()` and `cmd.ErrOrStderr()` in commands (instead of `os.Stdout` / `os.Stderr`) so output can be captured in tests.

## Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Writing to `os.Stdout` directly | Tests can't capture output. Use `cmd.OutOrStdout()` which tests can redirect to a buffer |
| Calling `os.Exit()` inside `RunE` | Cobra's error handling, deferred functions, and cleanup code never run. Return an error, let `main()` decide |
| Not binding flags to Viper | Flags won't be configurable via env/config. Call `viper.BindPFlag` for every configurable flag |
| Missing `viper.SetEnvPrefix` | `PORT` collides with other tools. Use a prefix (`MYAPP_PORT`) to namespace env vars |
| Logging to stdout | Unix pipes chain stdout — logs corrupt the data stream for the next program. Logs go to stderr |
| Printing usage on every error | Full help text on every error is noise. Set `SilenceUsage: true`, save full usage for `--help` |
| Config file required | Users without a config file get a crash. Ignore `viper.ConfigFileNotFoundError` — config should be optional |
| Not using `PersistentPreRunE` | Config initialization must happen before any subcommand. Use root's `PersistentPreRunE` |
| Hardcoded version string | Version gets out of sync with tags. Inject via `ldflags` at build time from git tags |
| Not supporting `--output` format | Scripts can't parse human-readable output. Add JSON/table/plain for machine consumption |

## Related Skills

See `samber/cc-skills-golang@golang-project-layout`, `samber/cc-skills-golang@golang-dependency-injection`, `samber/cc-skills-golang@golang-testing`, `samber/cc-skills-golang@golang-design-patterns` skills.

content.text:
All gates pass — the `catalog.go` formatting flag pre-exists my changes (a one-space alignment issue on the base branch; I left it alone since it's outside this change's scope). Full `go test ./...` is green, web typecheck and `make web` build cleanly.

## Done — the flow view is now a create surface

Everything from the approved plan is implemented on the new **`feature/flow-slot-create`** branch (off `feature/v-next`) and verified end-to-end in a real browser against a scratch workspace, including a real create against the official template library.

**Backend** (`internal/dashboard/`)
- `POST /api/templates/{name}/create` accepts an optional `dir` — a validated, root-relative, must-already-exist directory — so a block can scaffold into `acme/erp/order-extractor` instead of only the workspace root. `resolveCreate` keeps its security posture: every segment checked (no `..`, no hidden/empty segments, no backslashes) plus the absolute-path escape assertion, covered by a table-driven traversal test.
- `GET /api/templates` now also returns `entries` with each template's title, description, and labels (additive; `templates` unchanged), so the palette can filter by `intropy.dev/block-kind` in one request.
- New `GET /api/systems` lists every declared system, so a host-only system with zero blocks reaches the picker.

**Frontend** (`web/src/`)
- Three placeholder slots on the canvas — Extractor left, Core block middle, Loader right — low-contrast dashed cards that brighten on hover. The layout has a three-column floor so even an empty system renders as the fillable in→process→out skeleton.
- Clicking a slot opens `CreateDrawer.tsx`: templates filtered by block-kind label (with a "show all" escape hatch), the same form machinery as the Templates tab (now shared via `form.tsx`), and a locked `<systemPath>/` prefix on the output directory.
- Created-but-undeclared blocks render as **ghost nodes** (dashed, with a "scaffolded" tag) via the reverse of the existing scaffold↔topology join, and a neutral banner counts them with the `intropy sys create` hint plus the existing refresh button. After a create the drawer closes and the new ghost appears from a plain `/api/flow` re-fetch.
- Systems with scaffolds or only a host but no declared topology now appear in the picker and render the skeleton.
- One drive-by bug fix: `requestJSON` never attached the HTTP status to thrown errors, so the existing 409→force-checkbox flow in TemplatesView was dead code; errors now carry `status`.

**Verified in the browser**: skeleton + ghost rendering in both themes, a full create of a real extractor into `acme/erp/` (which also correctly scaffolded the `Contracts` dependency alongside), the ghost count updating to 2, and the empty `crm` skeleton. This also settled the plan's main open question — the official library's templates **do** carry `block-kind` labels; the extractor slot found its template on the first try.

**Good commit points** (proposing, not committing): this splits naturally into two — ① backend: `dir` on create + template labels + `/api/systems` with tests (`templates.go`, `handlers.go`, both test files), ② frontend: slots/ghosts/skeleton/drawer (`FlowView.tsx`, `CreateDrawer.tsx`, `form.tsx`, `api.ts`, `TemplatesView.tsx`, `index.css`). Say the word and I'll make them.

One known rough edge for the experiment, as planned: the transactional slot's middle-column position is a heuristic and can land beside topic nodes in wide graphs — worth flagging in the PR.

content.text:
Done — loader destinations now render on the right side of the system boundary.

**The change** (all in `buildDeclaredGraph`, `web/src/components/FlowView.tsx`): output ports used to drop *below* their component's column; they now sit on a destinations rail just past the boundary's right edge, aligned with the row of the component that writes to them, and bumped down when two would collide. The edge now leaves the component's right handle into the external's left handle, instead of bottom-to-top. Input ports are unchanged on the left, so the whole canvas now reads in → process → out end to end: sources → extractor column → topics → loader column → destinations.

**Verified visually against a real declared topology.** Since the scratch workspace had no buildable host, I gave its `erp-host` a tiny .NET console program whose graph verb prints a hand-written topology record — extractor with an input port, loader with *two* output ports. The canvas renders: `pim` source on the left, the pipeline through the `orders` topic, and `erp-api` + `audit` stacked on the right rail with edges from the loader. The stacking rule works (both destinations wanted the same row; the second bumped down). The ghost `order-extractor` and the slots still render correctly alongside the real declared graph, which also confirms the earlier slot/ghost work composes with a matched topology, not just the skeleton case.

Web typecheck and `make web` are green; no Go code changed this round.

One trade-off worth knowing: the old below-the-column placement existed to avoid long edges when a *mid-pipeline* component writes outward. With the rail, an out-port on a non-last-column component draws its edge across the downstream columns to reach the right edge. For the minimal topology scope (out-ports live on loaders, which are last-column) this doesn't arise, but if transactional blocks start declaring out-ports in wide graphs, we may want a "rail only for last-column components" refinement.

The commit proposal from before still stands, now with this included in the frontend commit — happy to make the two commits whenever you want.

content.text:
Done — topic nodes now render as a horizontal cylinder, the classic message-channel glyph, instead of a rounded card.

**How it's drawn**: the `TopicNode` in `FlowView.tsx` now carries an inline SVG behind its content — a silhouette path (rectangle with both ends bulging as elliptical arcs) plus a second arc that draws the near cap's seam on the left, which is what makes it read as a cylinder rather than a pill. The stroke keeps the accent color topics already had, the fill uses the surface token, and the seam is slightly faded so it reads as depth. The old card chrome (`background`/`border`) moves off the div onto the SVG in a new `.rf-topic-cyl` modifier in `index.css`, and the hub icon + topic/contract text float on top, padded past the seam. Handles, click-to-inspect, and edge attachment are untouched.

Verified in the browser against the fake `erp` topology in both themes — the `orders` cylinder sits between `pim-extractor` and `erp-loader` and is now clearly a different species from the component cards, in light and dark alike. `make web` (typecheck + build) is green; no Go changes.

One small note: because the SVG scales to the node's box (200×76), the cap curvature is tuned to that geometry — if `INFRA_W`/`INFRA_H` ever change, the `viewBox` and arc radii in `TopicNode` should move with them (they're side by side in the same file).

The two-commit proposal from before still stands, with this and the destinations rail folded into the frontend commit — say the word and I'll commit.

content.text:
Fixed — it was a missing `fill: currentColor`, not a color-token problem.

**Root cause**: the Material Symbols SVGs ship with no `fill` attribute, so their paths default to black. The three flow-node icon classes in `index.css` (`.rf-int-icon`, `.rf-infra-icon`, `.rf-ext-icon`) set `color: var(--accent)` / `var(--text-muted)` but never told the SVG to follow it — the app's generic `.icon` class has `fill: currentColor` for exactly this reason, but the flow canvas icons never used that class. So the icons were black everywhere: near-invisible on dark surfaces, and silently wrong (black instead of accent) on light ones.

**Fix**: added `fill: currentColor` to each of the three classes. Verified in the browser in both themes — component glyphs and the topic hub now render in the accent teal, external/resource cloud icons in the muted gray, clearly visible on the dark surface. Light mode also now shows the accent tint the CSS always intended, which is a small (intentional) visual change from before.

`make web` is green. This folds into the frontend commit along with the slots/drawer, destinations rail, and the topic cylinder — ready to commit whenever you want.

content.text:
Both done — an empty folder now opens as a fillable system, and it's named after the folder.

**Empty workspace renders**: the "No integrations to visualise." early return in `FlowView` is gone. When neither `/api/flow` nor `/api/systems` yields anything, the picker falls back to the workspace pseudo-system, so the canvas opens as the three-slot skeleton and the first block scaffolds at the workspace root (`dir: "."`). I verified the whole loop live: ran the dashboard on a brand-new empty folder, clicked the Extractor slot, created a real extractor from the drawer — it landed at the root (with its `Contracts` dependency) and came back as a ghost node with the re-sync banner.

**Folder as system name** (your follow-up): the server now includes the served root's directory name in `/api/health` (`"workspace": "ws-empty"`, resolved to an absolute path first so a relative root doesn't answer "."). The flow view fetches it and uses it as the pseudo-system's label — picker and boundary title both said **WS-EMPTY** instead of "Workspace" in the verification run. content.text:
I've read your implementation — nice contract (baseline from the host record, orphan diff, record rewritten last, conflicts refuse). My recommendation: **yes, wire it into the dashboard, but as the banner's one-click action rather than automatically inside every create.** Here's the reasoning:

**Why not auto-per-create:**

1. **Cost per click.** `Update` re-fetches the template tarball (network), re-renders the host, and `warnTopologyDrift` runs a dotnet build as its advisory check. Folding that into the create request makes every drawer submit slow and adds network/build failure modes to an action that's currently fast and local. And the canvas *still* shows a ghost afterward — wiring only appears after a topology refresh — so the user gains nothing visible for the wait.
2. **Batching.** Sketching a system usually means adding 2–3 blocks in a sitting. Auto mode does three host re-renders and three tarball downloads; a banner button folds all orphans in one pass — that's exactly the orphan-diff shape `planUpdate` already has.
3. **Failure honesty.** "Component created, host update failed" inside one request is a muddy response. Your own design is careful about honest baselines and refusing conflicts — keeping the two writes as two visible actions preserves that.
4. **The onboarding path breaks.** `planUpdate` requires an existing host — but the flow we just built lets you create the *first* block in an empty workspace or a system with no host yet. Auto-update would error on exactly the golden-path case; that situation needs `sys create`, not `sys update`.

**What I'd build instead:**

- `POST /api/systems/{path...}/update` → `system.Update` with `StartDir = root/<systemPath>` and captured stderr. One important detail from your implementation: `planUpdate` demands *exactly one* host under StartDir, so the endpoint must pass the system directory, never the workspace root (a multi-system workspace would error). The flow view's system key is already exactly that directory.
- The ghost banner becomes actionable: when the selected system has a host, "N scaffolded components not in the declared topology — **[Update host & refresh]**", which calls the update endpoint and then the existing topology refresh, so ghosts turn into declared, wired nodes in one click. When there's no host yet, keep the current `sys create` hint (a create-host button can be a follow-up).
- Serialize it with `createMu` like template creates, and map `ErrNoOrphans` to a friendly no-op.

Auto mode could still come later as an opt-in ("re-assemble after every create"), but I'd start explicit — it matches the plan/apply batching, and one click closes the whole loop.

Want me to build the endpoint and banner button?

1	// Package system assembles scaffolded integrations into a system host. It
2	// scans the workspace for the .intropy/scaffold.json records `int create`
3	// left behind, validates them into a system model, and builds the value
4	// payload the system-host template renders every declaration file from —
5	// Topics.cs, Ports.cs, the development and system definitions, and
6	// the csproj. The template library owns all generated content; this
7	// package owns workspace knowledge only.
8	package system
9	
10	import (
11		"context"
12		"encoding/json"
13		"fmt"
14		"io"
15		"net/http"
16		"os"
17		"path/filepath"
18		"strings"
19	
20		"github.com/huandu/xstrings"
21	
22		"github.com/integrio-intropy/intropy-cli/internal/template"
23	)
24	
25	// hostTemplate is the directory in the templates repo holding the system
26	// host: the shell plus every declaration file, rendered from the payload.
27	const hostTemplate = "system-host"
28	
29	type CreateOptions struct {
30		Name       string // system name as typed; PascalCase or kebab-case
31		StartDir   string // workspace scan root; default "."
32		OutputDir  string // default: the kebab-cased name
33		Version    string // template release tag; default: latest
34		Force      bool
35		OutputJSON string // path to write CreateResult JSON; "-" means stdout
36		Stdout     io.Writer
37		Stderr     io.Writer
38		HTTP       *http.Client
39		UserAgent  string
40	
41		// Owner and Repo select the template library; zero values target the
42		// official library. GitHubBaseURL is a test-only seam.
43		Owner         string
44		Repo          string
45		GitHubBaseURL string
46	}
47	
48	// minFactsPayloadVersion is the lowest template-library release whose
49	// system-host consumes the facts-only payload. Named in the version gate's
50	// error so a user on an older release knows the floor.
51	const minFactsPayloadVersion = "v0.4.0"
52	
53	// CreateResult is the machine-readable summary written when --output-json
54	// is set. Field names are stable and additive-only.
55	type CreateResult struct {
56		Template  string         `json:"template"`
57		Owner     string         `json:"owner"`
58		Repo      string         `json:"repo"`
59		Version   string         `json:"version"`
60		OutputDir string         `json:"outputDir"`
61		Values    map[string]any `json:"values"`
62		System    Summary        `json:"system"`
63	}
64	
65	// Summary describes the assembled system; it loosely mirrors the model the
66	// host's `graph` verb prints.
67	type Summary struct {
68		Name          string      `json:"name"`
69		Components    []Component `json:"components"`
70		Topics        []Topic     `json:"topics"`
71		Ports         []Port      `json:"ports,omitempty"`
72		SharedLibrary string      `json:"sharedLibrary"` // scaffold directory
73	}
74	
75	func (o *CreateOptions) applyDefaults() {
76		if o.StartDir == "" {
77			o.StartDir = "."
78		}
79		if o.Stdout == nil {
80			o.Stdout = os.Stdout
81		}
82		if o.Stderr == nil {
83			o.Stderr = os.Stderr
84		}
85		if o.UserAgent == "" {
86			o.UserAgent = "intropy-cli"
87		}
88	}
89	
90	// Create runs the full assembly: scan the workspace for scaffold records,
91	// validate them into a system model, build the value payload, and render
92	// the system-host template with it. All local validation happens before
93	// any network I/O.
94	func Create(ctx context.Context, opts CreateOptions) error {
95		opts.applyDefaults()
96		if opts.Name == "" {
97			return fmt.Errorf("a system name is required")
98		}
99	
100		// Exact parity with the templates' `{{ .name | kebabcase }}`: sprig
101		// delegates to xstrings, so OrderFlow and order-flow are equivalent.
102		kebab := xstrings.ToKebabCase(opts.Name)
103		if opts.OutputDir == "" {
104			opts.OutputDir = kebab
105		}
106	
107		entries, warnings := template.ListScaffolds(opts.StartDir)
108		for _, w := range warnings {
109			fmt.Fprintf(opts.Stderr, "warning: %v\n", w)
110		}
111		warnf := func(format string, args ...any) {
112			fmt.Fprintf(opts.Stderr, "warning: "+format+"\n", args...)
113		}
114		model, err := Assemble(entries, warnf)
115		if err != nil {
116			return err
117		}
118		model.Name = kebab
119	
120		payload, err := buildPayload(model, opts.OutputDir, kebab)
121		if err != nil {
122			return err
123		}
124	
125		if err := template.Create(ctx, template.CreateOptions{
126			Template:      hostTemplate,
127			OutputDir:     opts.OutputDir,
128			Version:       opts.Version,
129			SetValues:     payload,
130			Force:         opts.Force,
131			NoInput:       true, // the template's values come from the payload, never prompts
132			OnManifest:    requireFactsPayload,
133			Stdin:         strings.NewReader(""),
134			Stdout:        opts.Stdout,
135			Stderr:        opts.Stderr,
136			HTTP:          opts.HTTP,
137			UserAgent:     opts.UserAgent,
138			Owner:         opts.Owner,
139			Repo:          opts.Repo,
140			GitHubBaseURL: opts.GitHubBaseURL,
141		}); err != nil {
142			return err
143		}
144	
145		// The template derives projectName/systemClass from the name; reading
146		// them back from the record it just wrote keeps the result summary
147		// honest about what was rendered.
148		record, err := template.LoadScaffold(filepath.Join(opts.OutputDir, filepath.FromSlash(template.ScaffoldRelPath)))
149		if err != nil {
150			return err
151		}
152		hostEntry := template.ScaffoldEntry{Path: opts.OutputDir, Scaffold: *record}
153		if model.ProjectName, err = stringValue(hostEntry, "projectName"); err != nil {
154			return fmt.Errorf("template %s did not derive the host project name: %w", hostTemplate, err)
155		}
156		if model.SystemClass, err = stringValue(hostEntry, "systemClass"); err != nil {
157			return fmt.Errorf("template %s did not derive the system class name: %w", hostTemplate, err)
158		}
159	
160		contracts := "no contracts project"
161		if model.Shared != nil {
162			contracts = "contracts from " + model.Shared.Path
163		}
164		fmt.Fprintf(opts.Stderr, "assembled system %q: %d component(s), %d topic(s), %d port(s), %s\n",
165			model.Name, len(model.Components), len(model.Topics), len(model.Ports), contracts)
166	
167		return maybeWriteCreateResult(opts, record, model)
168	}
169	
170	// requireFactsPayload rejects a system-host template release that predates
171	// the facts-only payload: one that still requires sharedContracts consumes
172	// the pre-join payload shape (CLI-derived field identifiers and a csproj
173	// include path), which this CLI no longer produces. The gate runs before any
174	// output is written so an old release fails loudly instead of rendering a
175	// host that cannot compile.
176	func requireFactsPayload(t *template.Template) error {
177		required, _ := t.Spec.Parameters["required"].([]any)
178		for _, r := range required {
179			if name, _ := r.(string); name == "sharedContracts" {
180				return fmt.Errorf("system-host template %s requires the sharedContracts payload: it predates facts-only payloads (field identifiers and the csproj reference moved into the template) — use template release %s or newer", t.Metadata.Name, minFactsPayloadVersion)
181			}
182		}
183		return nil
184	}
185	
186	// sharedPath reports the detected contracts sibling for the JSON summary;
187	// empty when the workspace has none.
188	func sharedPath(m *Model) string {
189		if m.Shared == nil {
190			return ""
191		}
192		return m.Shared.Path
193	}
194	
195	func maybeWriteCreateResult(opts CreateOptions, record *template.Scaffold, model *Model) error {
196		if opts.OutputJSON == "" {
197			return nil
198		}
199		absOut, err := filepath.Abs(opts.OutputDir)
200		if err != nil {
201			absOut = opts.OutputDir
202		}
203		result := CreateResult{
204			Template:  hostTemplate,
205			Owner:     record.Owner,
206			Repo:      record.Repo,
207			Version:   record.Version,
208			OutputDir: absOut,
209			Values:    record.Values,
210			System: Summary{
211				Name:          model.Name,
212				Components:    model.Components,
213				Topics:        model.Topics,
214				Ports:         model.Ports,
215				SharedLibrary: sharedPath(model),
216			},
217		}
218		data, err := json.MarshalIndent(result, "", "  ")
219		if err != nil {
220			return fmt.Errorf("write --output-json: %w", err)
221		}
222		data = append(data, '\n')
223		if opts.OutputJSON == "-" {
224			if _, err := opts.Stdout.Write(data); err != nil {
225				return fmt.Errorf("write --output-json: %w", err)
226			}
227			return nil
228		}
229		if err := os.WriteFile(opts.OutputJSON, data, 0o644); err != nil {
230			return fmt.Errorf("write --output-json: %w", err)
231		}
232		return nil
233	}

content.text:
Done — the endpoint and banner button are built, and the full loop is verified end-to-end, including your mid-turn addition: **when the system has no host yet, the button runs `sys create` instead.**

**Backend** (`internal/dashboard/systems.go`): `POST /api/systems/{path...}` re-assembles one system's host the way the CLI would. It branches on `template.ListSystemHosts(dir)`: a host present → `system.Update` (your new orphan-fold, honoring the record's template pin); none → `system.Create` with the system named after its directory (the same rule that labels the pseudo-system) and the host rendered inside it as `<name>-host`. The path is validated with the same segment rules as create's `dir` and must exist; runs are serialized with `createMu`. The response says which verb ran (`action: update | create | none` — "none" is `ErrNoOrphans`, a successful no-op), plus `added`/`kept` and the command's stderr as diagnostics. Errors map to 409 (divergence, retryable with force), 422 (workspace-shape problems), 502 (template fetch). Three handler tests cover the no-orphans path, the create branch's pre-network validation, and encoded traversal (raw `../` never reaches the handler — the mux 307-normalizes it).

**Frontend**: the ghost banner's passive hint became the action. It reads "N scaffolded components are not in the declared topology yet" with a button labeled **Update host & refresh** or **Create host & refresh** depending on whether `/api/systems` knows a host there. One click: sync → topology refresh → ghosts become declared, wired nodes. After a create-branch sync it also re-fetches the flow and follows the selection onto the new system key, since a new host changes every sibling's grouping key (I hit that live — it briefly produced a duplicate picker entry before the fix).

**Verified against the real template library**: fresh empty folder → dashboard shows the `ws-empty` slot skeleton → created an extractor from the slot → banner offered *Create host & refresh* → click assembled `ws-empty-host` via real `sys create`, downloaded and built the actual .NET host, and the graph verb declared the component — the ghost turned into a declared `order-extractor` wired through the `orders` cylinder (`Contracts.Order`) with its source port outside. The catalog view also went from "identity from scaffold record" to a fully declared entry with contracts.

`go test ./...` and `make web` are green. This work sits uncommitted on top of your `caafaf53` — a natural commit would be "feat(dashboard): sync system host from the flow view" covering `systems.go`, the route, tests, `api.ts`, and the FlowView banner changes.
